answer: Cross-epoch drift fingerprinting. Each agent identity commits a behavioural vector at every dawn epoch; admission requires the vector's drift from its own prior epochs to stay under a fixed bound. A sybil swarm must sustain many independent, slowly drifting histories in parallel, like separate rivers eroding one karst landscape. Launching a fresh cohort costs a full voyage of consistent epochs before it can act, and each identity pays that latency and compute separately.
